name: Fu-En Yang
description: Fu-En Yang is a Research Scientist at NVIDIA Research advancing generalizable and agentic robot intelligence through robot agents and embodied reasoning, with a focus on self-improvement and zero-shot generalization.
bio: I am a Research Scientist at NVIDIA Research, advancing generalizable and agentic robot intelligence. My research interests center on robot agents, world–action modeling, and embodied reasoning, aiming to enable robots to learn from experience across embodiments, improve autonomously, and achieve zero-shot generalization across tasks and environments.

I received my Ph.D. from National Taiwan University in July 2023, advised by Prof. Yu-Chiang Frank Wang. Previously, I was a research intern at NVIDIA Research (Feb.–Aug. 2023) and a Ph.D. program researcher at ASUS AICS (Sep. 2020–Oct. 2022), working on model personalization, vision-language models, and visual transfer learning.
I received my bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from National Taiwan University in 2018.
research_interest: My research focuses on generalizable and agentic robot intelligence. I study how robot agents can integrate perception, world–action modeling, and embodied reasoning to understand how humans solve problems, reason about physical dynamics, and anticipate action outcomes. My goal is to build agents that plan over long horizons, self-improve through interaction, and achieve zero-shot generalization to new scenes, tasks, and embodiments.
